role: kick (inside mic) — LF thump + beater body. Bonham: keep WEIGHT; gentle de-box, no bright click.
rationale: Bonham wants weight, not click. HPF 30 + a -3 dB 31.5 Hz bell tames the sub-rumble shelf without touching the 58-63 Hz fundamental; -3 dB at 350 de-boxes (gentler than the warm recipe's -3.5 so the body stays). Only a small +1 dB at 4 kHz click (warm recipe used +2) — Bonham is dark. API comp New(FF) 3:1 Medium for body/slam; 550 top kept flat (hmf/hf = 0). declick off (percussive). Polarity left as the phase-align set it.

role: kick beater / click mic — owns attack. Bonham: it sits FAR under the room, so keep it gentle.
rationale: HPF 90 hands the thump back to the 'in' mic; -2.5/-3 at 200/340 kill cardboard box; +2 at 3 kHz beater click (BELOW the 5-7k harsh zone); -2.5 at 6 kHz + a gentle 5-7k de-harsh tame brittleness. Beater is ~10 LU under the room in the Bonham balance so this stays conservative. 550 top flat. No transient/excite (the room carries the life). declick off.

role: snare top — crack + body. Bonham: deep + FAT, ghost-note friendly. Keep body; do NOT gate.
rationale: Body-dominant (peak ~200 Hz). Bonham keeps the fat body: only a small -1.5 at 300 (warm recipe used -2.5) so the snare stays deep; -2 at 5 kHz de-spits the harsh nub; dynamic 3.5-6.5k de-harsh ducks ring only when it rings, leaving ghost notes intact. NO gate, NO transient snap (we want the natural body + ghost notes, not a modern crack), NO air (dark). API comp New(FF) 3:1 Medium for density; 550 top flat. Snare top sits under the room/OH in the balance. declick off; polarity left from phase-align.

role: snare bottom (wires) — buzz/snap. Bonham: a touch of wires under the top; far down in balance.
rationale: Wires mic: HPF 150 kills shell-ring/box LF junk; -4.5/-2.5 at 200/400 de-box; a modest +1.5 at 7 kHz (ABOVE the 5 kHz harsh edge, smaller than the warm recipe's +2.5 — Bonham is dark) presents the wire buzz, with 4.8-6.8k de-harsh guarding the edge. Sits ~13 LU under the snare top in the Bonham balance — just a hint of wires. 550 top flat (hf 0). declick off.

role: hi-hat (close mic) — salt-shaker hat. Bonham: barely present (OH/room carry the cymbals); NO air.
rationale: HPF 110 kills 63-80 Hz rumble/spill; -4.5 at 200 (single loudest band = whoosh/spill) and -3 at 400 clear the box; 5-7k de-harsh tames the brittle poke dynamically. KEY Bonham change vs the warm recipe: NO 11 kHz air shelf (the kit is dark and the OH/room own the cymbals) — the hat is pulled ~14 LU under the room in the balance. 550 top fully flat. declick off.

role: overheads (stereo) — cymbals + whole-kit image. Bonham: warm + dark, just under the room.
rationale: HPF only 120 (warm recipe used 140 — Bonham keeps more body) dumps the worst 63-80 Hz kick lump; just a gentle -1.5 at 200 to ease the box WITHOUT thinning the low-mid warmth (warm recipe cut -3 @200 + -1.5 @400 and brightened the bus — we deliberately keep the warmth); dynamic 3.15-6.3k de-harsh ducks cymbal/hat harshness only when it rings. KEY Bonham change: NO 12 kHz air shelf (warm recipe added +1.5) and hf gain 0 — keep it dark and natural. New(FF) 2.5:1 Medium comp for cohesion; 550 top flat. The OH carries the kit image just under the room.

role: room/ambience (stereo) — THE STAR (the 'reverb'). Bonham: keep it WARM, ALIVE, and big. Treat lightly.
rationale: The room is the Bonham sound, so treat it lightly and KEEP ITS LOW WEIGHT/WARMTH: HPF only 45 Hz (warm recipe used 50; we keep more bottom) and just ONE very gentle -1 at 210 to ease the worst box — deliberately NOT the warm recipe's -3.5 @210 + -2 @400, which would thin the body and brighten the bus. Light 2.5-6k de-harsh keeps it alive. Old(FB) 2:1 Medium comp at 0.3 s for character/glue WITHOUT crushing the natural dynamics (the room's huge crest IS the vibe). NO air. The room is pushed FORWARD in the balance (the loudest layer). declick off; polarity left from phase-align.
